edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Εἶτα τούτοις ἑξῆς παρακούσας ἤτοι τῶν ἱερῶν γραμμάτων ἢ τῶν μὴ νενοηκότων τὰ ἱερὰ γράμματά φησιν ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν λέγεσθαι μόνους διαμενεῖν κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ ἐπαχθησομένου τῷ κόσμῳ διὰ πυρὸς καθαρσίου οὐ μόνον τοὺς ζῶντας τότε ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς πάλαι ποτὲ ἀποθανόντας· οὐχ ὑπολαβὼν μετά τινος ἀποῤῥήτου σοφίας λελέχθαι παρὰ τῷ ἀποστόλῳ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τό· „οὐ πάντες κοιμηθησόμεθα, πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γὰρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.“ ἐχρῆν δ᾿ αὐτὸν ἐπιστῆσαι, τί νοήσας ὁ λέγων ταῦτα ὡς οὐδαμῶς νεκρὸς χωρίσας ἑαυτὸν ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνων καὶ τοὺς παραπλησίους ἑαυτῷ ἔλεγε μετὰ τὸ „καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι“· „καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.“ εἰς δὲ βεβαίωσιν τοῦ τοιαῦτά τινα νενοηκότα τὸν ἀπόστολον γεγραφέναι. ἃ παρεθέμην ἐκ τῆς πρὸς Κορινθίους προτέρας, παραθήσομαι καὶ τὰ ἐκ τῆς πρὸς Θεσσαλονικεῖς προτέρας, ἐν ᾗ φησιν ὁ Παῦλος ὡς ζῶν καὶ ἐγρηγορὼς καὶ ἕτερος ὢν τῶν κοιμηθέντων τοιαῦτα· „τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν λέγομεν ἐν λόγῳ κυρίου, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας, ὅτι αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος ἐν κελεύσματι, ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου καὶ ἐν σάλπιγγι θεοῦ καταβήσεται ἀπ᾿ οὐρανοῦ.“ εἶτα πάλιν ἑξῆς τούτοις ἄλλους ἐπιστάμενος τοὺς ἐν Χριστῷ νεκροὺς παρ᾿ ἑαυτὸν καὶ τοὺς παραπλησίους αὐτῷ ἐπιφέρει λέγων· „οἱ νεκροὶ ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστήσονται πρῶτον, ἔπειτα ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι ἅμα σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα.“
thought_title: Paul counts himself among the living
pass_a_gloss: Then next to these, having misheard (παρακούω) either the sacred writings (ἱερὰ γράμματα) or those who have not understood (νοέω, negated) the sacred writings, he says it is said by us that there will remain/survive (διαμένω) alone (μόνους), at the time (καιρός) of the cleansing (καθάρσιον) that will be brought on (ἐπάγω, fut. pass.) the world through fire (πῦρ), not only those living then but also those who died (ἀποθνῄσκω) long ago (πάλαι ποτέ) [Celsus's wording from 5.14]; not having supposed (ὑπολαμβάνω) that with a certain secret (ἀπόρρητος) wisdom (σοφία) was spoken by the apostle of Jesus: 'Not all shall we sleep (κοιμάομαι), but all shall we be changed (ἀλλάσσω), in an instant (ἐν ἀτόμῳ), in the blink (ῥιπή) of an eye, at the last trumpet (σάλπιγξ); for it will trumpet (σαλπίζω), and the dead will be raised (ἐγείρω) incorruptible (ἄφθαρτος), and we shall be changed.' He ought (χρή, impf.) to have attended (ἐφίστημι) to what the one saying this had in mind when, as being by no means (οὐδαμῶς) dead, he separated (χωρίζω) himself and those like (παραπλήσιος) him from those [the dead], and said after 'and the dead will be raised incorruptible': 'and we shall be changed.' For confirmation (βεβαίωσις) that the apostle wrote what I quoted (παρατίθημι) from the first [letter] to the Corinthians having understood some such things, I will quote also what is from the first to the Thessalonians, in which Paul, as living and awake (ἐγρήγορα) and being other (ἕτερος) than those fallen asleep, says such things: 'For this we say to you in a word (λόγος) of the Lord (κύριος), that we the living, those left behind (περιλείπομαι) unto the coming (παρουσία) of the Lord, shall by no means (οὐ μή) precede (φθάνω) those fallen asleep; because the Lord himself with a command (κέλευσμα), with an archangel's voice and with God's trumpet will come down (καταβαίνω) from heaven.' Then again next to these, knowing (ἐπίσταμαι) the dead in Christ to be others besides himself and those like him, he adds (ἐπιφέρω) saying: 'The dead in Christ will rise (ἀνίστημι) first; then we the living, those left behind, together with them will be snatched up (ἁρπάζω) in clouds to a meeting (ἀπάντησις) of the Lord into the air.'

choices.why: agency fixed: cleansing 'brought upon the world through fire', not 'which fire will bring'
Celsus quote rejoined in the 5.14 English wording; Origen's paraphrase 'we alone will survive' left unquoted
1 Cor 15:51-52, 1 Thess 4:15-16, 4:16-17 checked against the verses

pass_b_english: Next, having misunderstood either the sacred writings or those who have not understood the sacred writings, he says that we teach that at the time of the cleansing that will be brought upon the world through fire, we alone will survive, “not only those then living but also those who died long ago.” He did not grasp that it was with a certain secret wisdom that the apostle of Jesus said: “We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed” (1 Corinthians 15:51–52). He ought to have considered what the speaker had in mind when, as one by no means dead, he set himself and those like him apart from the dead, and after “and the dead will be raised incorruptible” said: “and we shall be changed.”

To confirm that the apostle had some such meaning when he wrote the words I have quoted from the First Letter to the Corinthians, I will quote also the words from the First Letter to the Thessalonians, where Paul, as one living and awake and other than those who have fallen asleep, says this: “For this we say to you by the word of the Lord, that we who are living, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will by no means go before those who have fallen asleep; for the Lord himself will come down from heaven with a word of command, with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God” (1 Thessalonians 4:15–16). Then again, right after this, knowing that the dead in Christ are others than himself and those like him, he goes on to say: “The dead in Christ will rise first; then we who are living, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air” (1 Thessalonians 4:16–17).
notes: Celsus is reported in indirect speech; Origen's μόνους διαμενεῖν (without Celsus's αὐτούς) is rendered as his paraphrase 'we alone will survive', unquoted; the phrase οὐ μόνον τοὺς ζῶντας τότε ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς πάλαι ποτὲ ἀποθανόντας repeats Celsus's words at 5.14 and is quoted in the same English wording used there ('not only those then living but also those who died long ago'). Reviewer: rendered τοῦ ἐπαχθησομένου ... διὰ πυρός as 'brought upon the world through fire' (fire is the means, not the agent). καθαρσίου is taken as the noun 'cleansing' (purification), governed by τοῦ ἐπαχθησομένου. σαλπίσει γάρ is impersonal in Greek ('it will sound'); rendered 'the trumpet will sound'. The staged text has a full stop after γεγραφέναι, which breaks one sentence; the translation reads εἰς βεβαίωσιν ... γεγραφέναι ἃ παρεθέμην ... παραθήσομαι as one sentence. ἐν κελεύσματι rendered 'with a word of command'.
Open doubt (review): 5.17: καθαρσίου could also be an adjective on πυρός ('through purifying fire'). The translator's noun reading ('cleansing') is kept; the sense is nearly the same.
